name: Long (Reverse) Iron Condor
summary: Buy the inner strikes and sell the outer strikes of both a call and put spread for a net debit; a defined-risk long-volatility bet that the underlying breaks out of a range.

legs.strike_rule: long put strike minus wing width W
long call strike plus the same wing width W

max_profit: (wing width W - net debit) x 100 per contract, achieved beyond either outer strike
max_loss: net debit x 100 per contract, if the underlying finishes between the two inner strikes
breakevens: lower BE = long put strike - net debit per share; upper BE = long call strike + net debit per share

greeks.theta: negative, roughly -1% to -2% of the debit per day at 45 DTE

when_to_use: IV rank <= 25 AND an identifiable catalyst inside the expiry (earnings, FDA date, macro print) or a volatility-compression setup: Bollinger Band width(20) in the bottom 15% of its 1-year range
entry_rules: Net debit <= 45% of the wing width W (otherwise the risk/reward is not worth it)
Inner strikes at 0.30-0.35 delta, wings equal width
Expected move (ATM straddle price / spot) must be LARGER than the distance from spot to the nearest inner strike, otherwise the structure can never pay
DTE 20-45; for an earnings play, the expiry immediately after the event
Debit paid <= 1% of equity per position
management_rules: Take profit at 100% of the debit paid (sell for 2x) or at 60% of max profit, whichever comes first
Volatility exit: if IV rank rises above 50 while the position is profitable, close immediately - the vega gain is the edge and it decays fast
Hard time stop: close at 10 DTE regardless of P/L; theta and the widening between the inner strikes destroy this structure late
Event exit: close within 30 minutes of the market open following a scheduled catalyst - IV crush after the event kills the position even if the move was right
No adjustments; this structure is either working or it is not
exit_rules: Force-close the entire structure by 15:45 ET on expiration day, always (the two short outer legs are assignable)
Close immediately if either SHORT outer strike goes ITM by more than 0.25 x W or its delta >= 0.85 - at that point the structure is at max profit anyway and holding only adds assignment risk
Ex-dividend guard on the short call
Abandon rule: if the position is down 70% of the debit with < 15 DTE, close and stop paying for time
assignment_risk: The two OUTER legs are short. They only go ITM when the trade is already at maximum profit, so the standard behaviour is: when a short outer strike goes ITM, take the profit and close, never wait.
buying_power: Net debit paid x 100 per contract (no additional margin; long inner strikes cover the short outer strikes).
liquidity_needs: Four legs must all be closeable; OI >= 500 per leg, spread <= 10% of mid. Wide markets eat the entire edge on a debit structure.
common_mistakes: Buying it when IV is already elevated; inner strikes too far apart so the required move is unrealistic; holding through the catalyst and getting crushed by the IV drop; paying more than half the width.
zero_dte_notes: Viable as a 0DTE breakout play on SPY/QQQ around 09:45-10:15 ET with inner strikes ~0.35 delta, but decay is brutal: set a hard 45-minute time stop and a 50% debit loss stop. Expect a low hit rate with large winners.
family: four-leg structures (iron condors, iron butterflies, condors, double calendars/diagonals, boxes, jelly rolls, conversions/reversals, double verticals, double ratio spreads)
